I got a refund for 'Cozy Grove'. The stuttery background visuals while moving around made me motion sick. It's a known issue, and there's very little you can do about it. Nothing worked for me. Now that I've played it for a while, I can even notice it in 'all' the videos. So look closely and be careful if that's something that makes you feel uncomfortable.

Other than that, the game seems to be exactly as advertised. Just keep in mind the very, very slow progression and the daily time gates, which received a special notice on the Steam page.
While i get this game would be for some people i disliked the UI and in general during the short time of playing it for the first time i just didnt have fun.

It's fine if you don't have a lot of time to play each day. I read the notice about it being 'optimized' for a couple hours of play, I didn't realize they lock the content so you can't continue more than one or two hours. It's not an optimization thing, all they're doing is forcing you to only do a limited amount of stuff to force you to play every day and it sucks. It's not about choosing to only play a little each day to make it last longer, you just can't advance after a few quests and since it runs on a 24 hour timer you HAVE to wait a full day until you can do anything else. That's not an 'optimization', that's stretching out an already thin amount of stuff to do to the point of being annoying. Not a fan, though the game would have been fun if not for that. Making you go slow because you don't have a lot of content is a cheap trick. Just tell people it's a short game and let them do them. As it is I have other games that don't restrict my fun so I'll play them and uninstall this. Glad I got it on sale at least. It's a game for people who have very short periods they can actually play a game, more like a mobile game than a computer game, I'm getting real tired of all the cross over games that are poorly designed for a computer, at least it's not a cash grab like the others.

This is one of those games where I wish there was a "neutral" recommendation rather than only 'yes' or 'no'. I would never recommend paying full price for this game because it's not worth $15. I bought this on sale for $6 and even then I'm struggling to justify the cost. I do think it will be okay to come back to every now and then when I'm bored of other games, but it's definitely not one you immerse yourself in or get attached to.

The Pros:
- the game is cute and cozy as advertised
- it looks like there will be some cute decorating and customizing of the little island which will be enjoyable
- the characters are adorable

The Cons:
- there's no keybind customization options
- the user interface is clunky
- feels like a mobile game
- tasks locked behind time (example: early game task locked behind 19 hour timer)
- basically just fetch quests over and over again

I'll add more as I continue playing because again, this is more of a neutral recommendation than a 'no', but the 'no' felt more fitting than a 'yes' in terms of my feelings. It'll still cure boredom for small increments of time and since it is a cozy game it's good if you want something simple and mindless to wind down.
beautiful game but it gets boring really fast

Editing a little over a month later- I've given this game a fair chance. Not only have I not changed my mind, I think I'm done entirely. This game is grindy, there's not enough to do, and you interact so little with everyone that it's too difficult to grow an interest in them. I'm not curious enough about any character to know what happened to anyone. I have animals including a cat in my house, I thought maybe that'd help, but it gets to the point they want expensive items to eat, I have multiple imps crying for expensive items, and quests have started taking 2+ days to complete. This game is not cozy or fun for me, I'm glad I'd only paid $5 so I don't have to sit here feeling ripped off for a game I tried so hard to enjoy.

Original review-

"Like Animal Crossing, Cozy Grove is synced to real world time, and provides 30-60 minutes of new quest content each day." 

Okay, look. I don't read the About This Game, I watch the trailer(s) and read reviews, I always assumed that'd tell me everything I need to know about a game. So that part's my fault. But the reviews restating "Hey this game works in realtime" didn't exist yet when I bought this. So if you're like me and go straight to the reviews- This game is cute but plays like the worst part about Animal Crossing. No, I do not want to sit here doing nothing but fishing because nobody else needs help for the day, and I just started playing so there's only so much to craft. 

It's almost insulting especially as a brand new player, I expect that from a free mobile game. I intend to continue playing, but it's going to be an occasional "Oh right, this game" as opposed to eagerly logging in each day. 

So if you're okay with maybe an hour of actual game per day, it's worth the sale price and it is indeed cozy, the art style is cute and the spirits are fun to get to know. But I'm too annoyed at "30-60 minutes of new quest content each day" to recommend it.

I wanted to love this game, but the controls just simply will not work. It takes pushing a button up to 12 times for it to register, and the joystick for moving is unresponsive most of the time. This game is unplayable with either PS or XBox controller. Incredibly frustrating.

Another game my past self bought and I regret now.

I want to love this game so much. The art, the atmosphere, and the music are wonderful. The design of the game, however, ruins it.

The first and most noticeable issue is the lack of instructions, even as the game progresses. For instance, one of my earliest quests told me to “look in piles of leaves.” So I searched and searched, only to eventually discover that the item could also be in stick piles or sand piles. The quest never mentioned that. The game never introduced the concept of piles by terrain type, nor did it give a quest that taught me the difference. So you’re left either poking around blindly until you stumble across it, or looking it up and feeling frustrated that the game didn’t bother to explain a basic mechanic.

The second issue is the “hidden object” quests. Yes, you get hints — but here’s the problem. Before you complete quests, most of the island is dull and colorless, and it’s absolutely cluttered with objects you can’t interact with. The landscape is busy, noisy, and hard to read. So when you get a quest like “find the blue leaves,” most of what you see isn’t actually blue, because it’s washed out in grayscale, or it’s buried behind other objects. You can tell the developers knew this was a problem, because they included an option to pay in-game currency to be led directly to the object. To me, that’s not a feature — it’s a band-aid for a design flaw.

The game also constantly gives you quests for things it has never introduced. I was asked to take a picture of the Cozy Grove sign with four wicker decorations. First problem: I didn’t even have a camera. No one gives you one, no quest introduces it — you’re just expected to somehow realize you have to buy it from the shop. Second problem: I have never once seen a wicker decoration. Not as a quest reward, not in the shop, not as a crafting recipe. Nothing. So I was left with a full day where a time-sensitive quest could not be completed through no fault of my own.

It’s the same with food. My spirit bird constantly asks for “acorn flour,” but the game never once explains how flour is made or where to make it. I am assuming the baker bear is the one who would make it or help you make it but that option is not available so I as stuck not being able to feed the spirit bird, thinking I was missing something obvious, when in reality the mechanic wasn’t available to me at all and without the item derived from feeding the bird, another quest was blocked.

This isn’t about being “bad” at the game. It’s about a game that refuses to explain its own mechanics, then punishes you for not knowing what it never taught you. It makes you feel like you’re the problem, like you’re stupid for not figuring it out — when really, it’s the game that’s broken.

If Cozy Grove wants to be truly cozy, it needs clear guidance, fair quests, and a system that doesn’t demand items you literally can’t access yet. Until then, it’s just a beautiful package wrapped around frustrating, confusing design.
Boring.

The premise is cute, the graphics are fun and pleasant to look at but I have no desire to play this game. I was hoping it would bring me back and enchant me more but it felt like an shlog. I could not just sit and play, I had to wait a day to progress, no thank you. It almost felt like it was going to dive into a gacha game. I could tell inventory management was going to be a pain and that it would take a lot of grinding to get things. Items blended to well into the backgrounds and were hard to spot. After running around a tiny island multiple times for 1 item, I was over it.
Not what I was hoping for. I can understand why many people enjoy this game but it's not for me.

I remember the game devs from the early 10's with a playstore/mobile game called Cozy Grove. In the style of 2048, you merged three of the same to increase it's value- except instead of numbers, you were working with the evolution of progress. From trees to log houses, to castles: you needed to build as high as you could go without letting the bears that would wander the board prevent and destroy progress. It was a cute game that resulted from joining the band wagon; similarly, this game has done much the same but not nearly as fun and with far more grinding to it.

I don't recommend this unless you like the daily mechanic from moneytrap mmos.

its bad alternative to animal crossing, the biggest problem with this game is clarity. you can't tell what you can harvest and what's decor, they're just too similar looking, you'd end up spam clicking everything to find what you need. not only that but the requests are too demanding, you need so much of one thing to craft another. the gameplay loop isnt satisfying enough. 
although i'll admit catching bugs and fish is fun but it falls again to due clarity once again, the bugs aren't unqiue looking, so many of them have recolours, each recolour is a "rare" or "common" so if you wanna catch all bugs, you'd have to catch them three times. Unlike animal crossing or hell any game with catching fish or bugs, where the rare fish actually look different with a different model. 
Plus having to log in everyday and seeing your island be white and black EVERYTIME is annoying, you'd have to complete the daily quests for coloured background, it seems so annoying to me. 
I wanted to enjoy this game and i tried several times, but it's just bad. i wish i can refund it but i spent too much time ingame to realize that its not that good

Game is fun. Well thought out. There are some glaring problems. 
- You up grade your campsite and island store. The cost for the store goes from 10 000 to 100 000 or 200 000 that is pretty excessive jump. 
- You can only play this game for 30-60 minutes a day. If I had known that, I would not have bought the game. When I buy a video game, I want to be able to play it as much or as little as possible. 
- I have 3 days or longer worth of play time, trying to find one item for a quest. Cannot find it. Even watched a few you tube videos. Not where the videos said it would be. I don't know if this is by design, or a bug. 
- Other reviewers have commented on how hard it is to find items. And yes at times, it is extremely difficult.
- You get a net, and you have to catch bugs. In a normal game, you would just walk up to a bug, and swing your net and catch the bug. But, nope, you have to throw your net. You could be standing right next to a bug, throw the net, and miss. The game is just full of dumb ideas like this one. And if you do it wrong, you walk in a direction you did not want to, and spook the bug.
- You have to buy a camera, and set the scene by placing items on the ground to get pics, for certain characters. If I want to move the camera up, I have to move the mouse down. If I want the camera to pan left, I have to move the mouse right. Another dumb (*)&)(* idea from the developers. I don't know, why not just allow players to move the camera normally. I want to pan left, so move the mouse left..... 

A person with the mind of a 3 year old could have done better in certain parts of the game.

The game has me running around searching for hidden items. Due to the artstyle, it's really hard to see anything. Items don't stick out from the environment and it's hard to tell what can be picked up or interacted with. I can only see this getting more confusing as the game goes on and you start cluttering the area with placeable objects. I just found it confusing and frustrating due to this.

less than 30 mins of actual game play and then you have to sit and wait for next real time day to do anything and then the cycle repeats. the game is cute and has potential but just nothing to do or missions take days (real time) to complete. this game tries to be Animal Crossing but fails horribly.

Not fun or chill. Just a series of repetitive fetch quests in a small area. Tasks like fishing and rock skipping are way harder than they need to be. And the interface is very annoying when interacting with objects.

Don’t get me wrong it is a very cozy and cute game, but unlike animal crossing and stardew valley it’s just extremely repetitive. The backgrounds are way too much to look at and it’s always a hassle to find any quest items, managing resources for the game is hard as well because the bears demand more and more each time, not a lot gives you money besides growing things, the bears are also very repetitive and you don’t really get to know much about them until a certain level of hearts. If you like animal crossing I cannot recommend this and instead would recommend slime rancher. Love the art style of this game but it just isn’t a good one unfortunately.

Having played over 40 hours and unlocked over 8 bears, I can safely say this game isn't for me. Not enough variety in what you can do.  Very little planning involved. There is some kind of story here about spirits, but nothing with any real tension, surprise, or consequence in terms of choices later. Large majority of stuff you can craft does nothing except help some trees or bushes to grow. The most tedious part is inventory management since you cap out how much storage you may use, which  based on your coin economy, but because so many quests require you to buy expense clothing or decorations, I felt like I had to constantly convert things into other things just to save some space in my backpack and in my camp storage. Too tedious for too little gain.

I think a lot of the issue for me might be that when you're looking for things to interact with (a dirt pile to dig, a rock to mine, etc), it all blends in with the background a bit too much. I just don't really feel like I'm doing a whole lot of anything when I'm trying to complete objectives in the game. I may need to collect a specific resource, and there's not really anything to do while you're roaming around. It mostly feels like you're just wandering around, and the objectives just aren't satisfying for me.

I tried to like this. I really, really tried. But ultimately, I just couldn't.
There's various things I could say about all the little annoyances and mild tedium in the game, but the main issue for me boils down to one thing: the way the camera pans around as the character moves gives me motion sickness. And a lot of the gameplay involves running around the island searching for things. As the island gets bigger and more populated, you do a lot more running around, which makes me getting motion sickness inevitable.
So yeah. It's a good concept, but I just can't handle the camera pan motion.

Super cute, comfy game, but very much not for me. I have a lot of trouble finding the items required to progress, they just hide in the environment.

This game could have been fun if it wasn't time locked. If you want a game to get lost in for hours until you finish it, this is not the game for you. You can only play the game for a couple of hours a day because it will literally stop progressing and tell you to either decorate your camp (which is mid) or come back tomorrow. 

I ended up returning it after playing it for a day and not being able to progress, When I looked it up on reddit, so many people have been saying they love the game and have been playing for 2 YEARS, and I'm just not interested in that kind of game.

As a disgusting completionist, Cozy Grove is a nightmare. The daily grind and unchangeable villagers are a pain. You have to feed and harvest animals of each tier 500 times, and animals don’t want to be fed everyday. You have to mend 200 broken heart imps for the max badge. That’s 200 days of gameplay [i]AND[/i] that’s if you can get [b]BOTH[/b] imps to spawn. I’ve constantly been victim to single heartbroken imps spawning, so I can’t even complete that badge within 200 days. On top of that, you need 30 birds, 30 deer, 20 “bunnies”, 150 decorations, 150 flowers, and 100 fruit trees to finish the decoration badges collection. Do you want to know what that’s like? I have to hoard the floral and fauna and I’ve had the Unity crash screen when I decide to perform one too many actions with all of this junk on the screen. [spoiler]Also, in my so-called “cozy” grove, I’m stuck with a conspiracy theorist and a greedy capitalist. How can I even relax or whatnot playing a game where I go on wild goose chases for a tin foil hatter and run errands for a finance bro paying me peanuts??[/spoiler] I’m so far in I have to finish these badges but I would not recommend this game for the faint of heart.

If you do decide to get the game, read the subreddit, the people on there are godsends. How would I have known that tinctures are the best way to make money? How would I have known the food combinations to get good cats?

Meh. I play this when I have nothing else to play. It’s kind of slow and can be boring. The characters are bland. The crafting system is such a chore. They also have hidden the second game behind a Netflix subscription. No thanks. 

Tl;dr it’s cute but there’s other games you can play in this genre that are less sluggish and tedious.

the little costumes you can get are cute - dead bears are cute - its mostly fetch quests and scavenger hunts but once you get in the groove you have to wait for the next day irl to progress and all i wanna do is sleep in my tent to advance time. otherwise i would have kept playing it (i don't have the mental fortitude to come back to things)
i liked the game well enough but the gameplay was kind of lacking, though this might be a user issue

I really wanted to like this game and there are many things about the game that I do like, but there more that I don't like. This game eats time which can be great if that's how you want to spend your time, but doing the daily errands can easily consume two or more hours. 
The music is good! The graphics are lovely. 
The game is unnecessarily "clicky". There are some tasks, like having items cataloged, which could be done in just a couple of clicks, but end up taking significantly more than necessary. Almost every interaction involves unnecessary clicks. 
The game area is far too cluttered and as you continue to play you end up adding to that clutter. That clutter can make it difficult to find items and or interact with items when needed. 
When dealing with most of the ghost bears if you craft something you get it immediately, but with the baker whatever you made gets delayed sent to the postal worker. 
You're encouraged and need to have a lot of pets and you need to feed them and what they might want can vary. As a result you can end up spending a lot of time running back and forth to the baker and the postal worker and "Flamey" in order to get things from your inventory.
Inventory is a problem. As you play the game there is an ever increasing number of items most of which you need to keep because you're going to need it to craft something later or it's an item that will be needed for a quest later. You can increase the amount of inventory space you have by increasing your tent and/or increasing what Mr. Kit's store has to offer all of which costs money. Catching fish and burning them and then crafting the bones into an item that sells for a good price is the easiest way I found to make money so it is possible even early in the game to increase your available inventory it is just time consuming and that doesn't always add to the enjoyment. 
I really wanted to like this game. If the "daily tasks" could be completed within a half hour to 45 minutes, I probably would have even with the clutter and excessive inventory needs and clicky interface. As it is, I have more important things to do and I don't like this game enough to continue with it. 
Pity, it could have been a really good game.

Really wish I'd known this was a time gated game before buying it. *sigh* Oh well, on to something else. If you like being told, in your big age, how much time you're allowed to play a game before it "runs out of stuff to do for the day" then look no further. Ain't nobody got time to be changing the time on their pc just to play a game, ffs.

I would say this game has the potential to be the worst game on Steam. Keep it up. Boring, no gameplay, no story. You only get to play for one or two hours, and then you have to wait until the next day? What is this, a mobile game?
It is a bit underwhelming for me and restricted so I wouldn't really recommend it but it isn't bad to be honest

I have mixed feelings about this game after nearly 20 hours of playtime.  I like the art style, the different characters you meet, and the fact that it's a good way to spend the first 30 minutes of my morning while I wake up.  I played it daily for a little while, until the fetch quests got more difficult to complete in a reasonable amount of time (took me like a week for one of them).  After awhile of playing everyday, the gameplay got dull, the items got more difficult to see when I was looking for them (the background is all the same color), and I lost interest in adding anything to my camp.  It was fun for a little while, but I just can't recommend this game at it's current pricing.  If you still want the game after reading this review, wait for a sale.

I have mixed feeling on the game. Definitely took me a while to learn the mechanics of being a ghost scout and making items. Maybe the game needs more direction early on. Also lot easier to navigate the world with just the mouse since you just click on items and people to interact. It does have qualities that are like Animal crossing since its real time and you need to come back daily for progress. Very cutie game and might be great for others.

i love the game a lot!! super cute and had lots of fun.. just the further you get into the game the more outrageous and stupid the quests get. you either have massive fetch quests where you have to run around the island for like 50 items, waiting for an item from another npc or they ask for like 20 silver ingots yet with the respawn time of ores etc. it just takes way too many real days to get the stuff. made me stop playing because progressing was just impossible. it seems like their only way of progressing the difficulty of the quests is make it more items but with the real time aspect of this game its just not a vibe. if they could add some variety to the quests that would be better!

I was expecting a game where you explore new locations & help the spirits along the way - something like Spiritfarer. Instead I've got "go grab this, bring me that" type of gameplay - the game basically consists of fetch quests only. And not just fetch quests, it's kind of "Where's Wally" kind of fetch quests where you gonna break your eyes trying to see that uncolored quest item among the same uncolored items. 

Graphics, sound & music production are absolutely incredible, but dear god this game is under-stimulating & boring and just won't let you enjoy it for more than 2 hours.
A game I really wanted to love but just can't. I always feel like I could be playing other games every time.

I can see how others have found this game relaxing and pleasant. It's got a great style and is super chill. For me, though, it was too boring. After a couple days, I had no desire to open it back up. It was just too repetitive and slow and there wasn't enough story progression to keep me coming back. In Cozy Grove, the only goal really is "help the spirits." I know that it apparently has some kind of nice story, however, after playing for a couple days there was no real story progression. Just access to more items and things to find. I guess I just need a little more brain food/stimulation with my games. But again, I do see how some people would like it. It's definitely a game that you can turn your brain off with. Just not my cup of tea.

This game is not necessarily bad per se, rather charming and cute in it's own unique way.
However, as someone who is an avid animal crossing fan (400+ hrs into new horizons), I found Cozy Grove quite disappointing in what it promises. Most of the customization items are locked behind finding random macguffins scattered across the tiny island, which would not be a problem in concept.

However, Cozy Grove game play takes inspiration from Animal crossing daily "quest" line system. In which the player can only invest so much daily, before having to put the game down to await a reset. Yet, as a lover of the former, time skipping is a concept and Cozy Grove does not have the same solution. Thus, putting a barrier on what could be a long session, restricted solely for short bursts of play time.

There is so much tension into the market place with npcs as well, instead of a wholesome leisure time it's rushing from point a to point b, trying to be diligent on which choice will benefit the player in the little time they are afforded. 

My review is not made in ill will towards the team, as they have a good concept on their hands. The last comment made by myself, is that I would have appreciated the constructive feedback they have gotten of how to fix the glaring problems into cozy grove itself; rather than their exclusive deal with netflix, where subscription havers on IOS will get their Cozy Grove sequel (Cozy Grove: Camp Spirit) that will be a polished Cozy Grove.

Sigh... I'm so disappointed. What have you become, Spry Fox?

I really wanted to like Cozy Grove. In theory, it has so much I love in a game: slow but steady progression, collecting and harvesting, decorations. It's one of the few games that borrows from Animal Crossing in which it's in real time, and you're rewarded for playing every day in it. On paper, it seemed like a mix of Animal Crossing, Spiritfarer and Story of Seasons. You get pets! You have sets to decorate your house and town with! You can cook! All the while helping the Grove's spirits and learning more about their backstory.

The theory is great. The execution... Not so much. It's an okay game, but it's stretched thin and meant to be played for 100+ days, when the endgame is painfully empty. And none of the features I talked about are very rewarding. I'll get to it.

I had a great time in the first 10 hours or so. So much, I got excited, I bought the DLC. I'm now sitting at 80 hours gameplay and have not been able to start it, as the dlc only starts once the main quests have been done. All well, I don't mind putting a lot of hours in a game, as long as it's enjoyable. And here, it's just not the case.

As I said, the game is designed and there's hardly anything to do after day 30 or so... It becomes a drag, you keep on farming but there is nothing else to do. I guess feeding the bird again to get your 432nd essence. 

What you're really waiting for, though, is the story. But even then, it feels like the bears are just stalling to say anything meaningful. They'll ask for you to catch 5 rare fish for the 10th time (their quests are also repetitive) so they'll tell you their story. What do they say? Quote one of the characters (spoilers ahead!):

Hardly a soul survived the accident. Not even mine.
Huh? Ye want me to continue my story, do ye?
Arr, I see. One good line isn't enough.
Well then. I'll tell ye the next part... soon.

That's all you get. One line. Want to hear more? You'll need to wait a few days. All stories are painfully stretched thin, stalled and worked up when there's not much content really. I caught myself skipping dialogues more often than not -- something I NEVER do in games! 

The other features are not much fun either. Cooking is pretty simple, gathering resources has awfully long animations (no, I don't want to see my character and all of her pets dance after I've plucked my 597th flower), the fish and bugs in the game are also artificially made more varied: 4-5 bugs will have exactly the same design, the same description but different colors. I'd much rather have 20 original species than 20+80 reskins...

Well, at least you get to decorate your home and town, right? Not so fast... Your pets and cats have opinions and will love you based on what you used to decorate. Both my home and the Grove became a haphazard clutterfest and any decorating projects I might have end up becoming too convoluted for me to even start. 

Long story short, this game tries to get inspiration from animal crossing, but in all the wrong way. Due to many of their game design choices, it ends up feeling more like a lazy free-to-play mobile or facebook game than anything else. It made me wonder if the devs even played their own game to the end. 

That being said, there still are a lot of people who love and enjoy it as it is. I think it's enjoyable if you don't mind playing it for 20 hours or so and then dropping it when it inevitably becomes dull and chore-y.

For the completionists like me, even if you enjoy the genre... Don't. Trust me. You're going to have a bad time.

I really hate it when cozy games let the villagers treat you like absolute crap and be extremely rude to you, yet leave you with no other option than to be placidly railroaded by them. It's like a Retail Customer Service position except you don't get paid.

I'm really torn on this one, but ultimately leaning towards negative. The reason being that I ended up quitting the game before I really wanted to. 

[u]The game has a lot of positives going on for it:[/u]
-Cool art style
-The game is just oozing with atmosphere - especially at night
-Love the sound design too
-Most of the minigames work well enough. I especially like fishing and skipping stones

[u]but there are some negatives too:[/u]
-It's essentially a game of fetch quests. If you don't like the minigames, this is gonna be horrible for you
-The coziness thing feels a bit forced. It's oozing with atmosphere, yes, but it's not that cozy. I especially found the ability to hug the bears kinda tacked on. As if some higher-up who's completely out of touch with the playerbase in the publishing company forced them to add it or something (which probably isn't the case, since this is an indie game, but that's how it feels)
-The controller support is super buggy. Sometimes the character won't stop moving and sometimes it won't stop using things you're carrying etc. This does not happen in other games, so the controller is fine
-The economy of the game is all over the place. You get a few coins as a reward when you do quests, but you can't buy anything with that. Sell a couple useless items at the shop and you've gained hundreds of coins in no time. What's the point of the quest rewards? Also, upgrading your tent, on the other hand, is ridiculously expensive

[u]but the biggest issue of them all[/u] is the inventory management. Good Christ almighty, you have like a million different "skills" or activities and each of them has several tiers of items related to them. You can upgrade your storage space via the ridiculously expensive tent upgrades and apparently there's some options for bags and stuff, but boy, does the constant stress about inventory space kill any chance of the game feeling COZY. 

But despite this, I do have some good memories with the game. I remember playing the game at night last Christmas. Just chilling there and fishing. And then it started snowing. It was truly cozy for a moment.

This game was a tentative positive, but after the devs actions it has become a 100% negative. 
First why a tentative positive: I liked the game's feel and aesthetics, also the seasonal items offer a lot of replay potential and the controls are nice (a fishing game that doesn't suck?). Then there's stuff that I didn't like. Not a fan of the limited gameplay simply because I have very little free time to play, and when I do I tend to engage in long playing sessions - it can't be done with this game. Also didn't like having to carry around quest items for days when inventory is so limited - one of my rooms basically became a hoarder's house. Also, some of the characters  are insufferable. Finally, resources sometimes felt unbalanced, with some hard to find items required for menial tasks - my animals went hungry more than once. 
What I REALLY didn't like was the dev admitting to G*mesR*dar that they learnt a lot from the players on how to make their game better, and then decided to release their supposedly better sequel behind a monthly subscription paywall (for a game with seasonal items and limited daily gameplay) that can only be played on mobile. Thanks for the eff you and right back at you. Glad I didn't buy the DLCs, this studio doesn't deserve any more of my money.
